The Rogers Park fire victims were identified by relatives as Valentino Vallejo, 13; Francisco Vallejo, 24; Mariza Garcia, 48; and Maria Jimenez de Garcia, 69.

Jim Urquhart/For the Sun-Times

Share

It was 6 a.m. Thursday when sisters Angelita Sanchez and Vanessa Garcia learned through a news report the Rogers Park townhome where their sister, mother and two nephews lived was on fire.

They later received the devastating news that their relatives had died.

The victims were identified by relatives as Valentino Vallejo, 13; Francisco Vallejo, 24; Mariza Garcia, 48; and Maria Jimenez de Garcia, 69.

For Sanchez, the tragedy is also the loss of a family matriarch who held her daughters together, particularly after their father died during the COVID-19 pandemic.

“We’re women power. She was the head of the woman power,” Sanchez said of her mother. “We’re family bound.”

A day later, as relatives searched their charred home at 7049 N. Paulina St. for belongings and keepsakes, neighbors and strangers stopped to offer condolences, prayers and donations.

Among them was Ellen Baren, who lives a couple of blocks away. Although she didn’t know the family, the news of the fire and the deaths hit her deeply. She walked to the home to pay her respects, but began to cry as she approached.

“It’s sad because all of a sudden it started and all of a sudden, you know, it was over. Their lives were over,” Baren said.

Standing across the street, Baren sang a Jewish prayer: “May your memory be for a blessing.”

“The prayer isn’t so much about someone passing away as much as it is to live a good life,” Baren said.
